name: go-vendored-dep-missing-selector-asks
desc: `text.Lower` on a vendored external package that exports only `Upper`. Vendoring is what makes this hermetic: with vendor/modules.txt present the index resolves imports from vendor/ and nothing else, so "the package resolved and lacks this symbol" is a fact the fixture states rather than one inherited from the machine's module cache or GOROOT. The load-bearing assertion is expect_log_reason: before #268 this logged as "violations", and deleting `fired.DepsGo = len(dv) > 0` left the whole suite green — the same unpinned-bucket hole as qualified.json's first case

name: go-unresolvable-dep-abstains-clean
desc: `missing.Nosuch` on a package that is imported but NOT vendored: the index returns Unknown rather than Resolved, and the check must fail silent. Pins the `pkg.Res != depindex.Resolved` bail — remove it and an unresolvable package reads as an EMPTY package, so every call into it is a violation. That is the check's worst failure mode in practice, because unresolvable is the normal state on a machine with a cold module cache, and it would fire on correct code
